Case: North America's Building Trades Unions v. Department of Defense

status_summary: DoD issued a class deviation on 2025-02-07 directing contracting officers to stop using project labor agreements on large-scale construction, the VA issued a similar deviation on 2025-02-20, and GSA issued a class exception for land port of entry projects. On 2025-05-16 the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia preliminarily enjoined the DoD and GSA memoranda in North America's Building Trades Unions v. Department of Defense; a litigation clearinghouse reports the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case on 2025-07-07. OMB Memorandum M-25-29 of 2025-06-12 stated that Executive Order 14063 remains in effect, that blanket deviations are precluded and earlier deviations should be rescinded, and that the administration supports project labor agreements when practicable and cost effective, while widening the cost and competition exceptions. An August 2026 CRS In Focus describes the order and its FAR rule as still in place, so the operative policy keeps the requirement the Mandate's alternative view would end. No Davis-Bacon repeal action was found.

timeline.event: DoD issued a class deviation directing contracting officers to end the use of project labor agreements on large-scale construction projects.

title: End mandatory project labor agreement requirements on federal construction
uncertainties: The court order, the docket and the agency deviations were not opened (the court docket host refuses automated fetches); the injunction comes from the American Bar Association, Economic Policy Institute and Government Executive accounts, which agree, and the dismissal from a litigation clearinghouse summary, whose outcome field oddly lists the defendants as prevailing. The CRS In Focus of 2026-08-12 (date from its file name) does not discuss the 2025 agency actions; it reports a separate Eleventh Circuit challenge to the order, affirmed against the challengers in April 2026 and pending on a rehearing petition. A September 2026 FAR overhaul proposal (parts 14, 28, 36 and 52) was read in part by the researcher and no project labor agreement text was found, but truncated Part 36 text means a change there is not ruled out. Diverged rather than blocked is a rubric judgment: the widened exceptions in M-25-29 may reduce project labor agreement use in practice, which could be read as limited movement toward the recommendation. The Mandate presents this item as an alternative view, so alignment is partial.
